about: The realms of 300 BC (decisions 'Playable 1' and '30': borders redrawn by us from open knowledge, any realm playable). Each realm lists the historical districts it held (name, lon, lat, and optionally how far in km it reaches when nothing else is near; 260 km by default, 340 for tribal peoples, counted in 'rough km': a km of mountain, marsh or desert counts for more); tools/build_realm_mask.py grows each district over the land, slowed by mountains, marsh and desert, until it meets its neighbours, and bakes data/political_mask.png. Where no district reaches, the land is unclaimed. tribal: a confederation of peoples, not an administered state, so it starts without provinces. law: male (male-preference primogeniture) or any (plain primogeniture). Rulers and families as attested; where the sources name no one (most tribal peoples and republics) the ruler stands for the leading family and bears a name of the culture. Sources: the Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World (Talbert, 2000); the Cambridge Ancient History VII.1 (1984); Diodorus, Plutarch, Justin, Polybius. Our own data, free for any use.

realms.name: Rome
realms.note: The Republic with its Latin, Campanian, Marsic, Apulian and Picene allies (the Picentes allied in 299 BC). Its 'ruling family' stands for the leading house, the Valerii.
realms.blurb: A modest city-state on the Tiber, one power among many on the Italian peninsula. History remembers what it became - not what it started as.

realms.name: Samnite League
realms.note: The Pentri, Caudini, Hirpini and Frentani; Gellius Egnatius led them in the Third Samnite War (298-290 BC).
realms.blurb: The Pentri, Caudini, Hirpini and Frentani; Gellius Egnatius led them in the Third Samnite War (298-290 BC).

realms.name: Etruscan League
realms.note: The twelve cities of Etruria with their Umbrian allies, who fought Rome together at Sentinum (295 BC).
realms.blurb: The twelve cities of Etruria with their Umbrian allies, who fought Rome together at Sentinum (295 BC).

realms.name: Cisalpine Gauls
realms.note: The Boii, Insubres, Cenomani, Lingones and Senones of the Po valley.
realms.blurb: The Boii, Insubres, Cenomani, Lingones and Senones of the Po valley.

realms.name: Lucanians and Bruttians
realms.note: The Oscan-speaking Lucanians and their Bruttian offshoot.
realms.blurb: The Oscan-speaking Lucanians and their Bruttian offshoot.

realms.name: Messapians and Peucetians
realms.note: The Iapygian peoples of Apulia's heel.
realms.blurb: The Iapygian peoples of Apulia's heel.

realms.name: Tarentum and the Italiote League
realms.note: Tarentum led the Greek cities of Italy; it called in Pyrrhus against Rome in 281 BC.
realms.blurb: Tarentum led the Greek cities of Italy; it called in Pyrrhus against Rome in 281 BC.

realms.name: Syracuse
realms.note: Agathokles, king of Sicily since 304 BC, married Theoxene, Ptolemy's stepdaughter, c. 300 BC.
realms.blurb: Agathokles, king of Sicily since 304 BC, married Theoxene, Ptolemy's stepdaughter, c. 300 BC.

realms.name: Massalia
realms.note: A Greek republic run by its council of six hundred (the timouchoi).
realms.blurb: A Greek republic run by its council of six hundred (the timouchoi).

realms.name: Gallic Tribes
realms.note: A world of tribes, not a state: the Arverni, Aedui, Sequani, Volcae and their neighbours.
realms.blurb: A world of tribes, not a state: the Arverni, Aedui, Sequani, Volcae and their neighbours.

realms.name: Celts of the Danube
realms.note: Celtic peoples settling Noricum and Pannonia; Kambaules led them into Thrace c. 298 BC.
realms.blurb: Celtic peoples settling Noricum and Pannonia; Kambaules led them into Thrace c. 298 BC.

realms.name: Iberian Peoples
realms.note: The Ilergetes, Edetani, Contestani, Bastetani, Oretani and Turdetani.
realms.blurb: The Ilergetes, Edetani, Contestani, Bastetani, Oretani and Turdetani.

realms.name: Celtiberian Peoples
realms.note: The Arevaci, Belli, Carpetani, Vettones, Vaccaei, Cantabri, Astures and Vascones.
realms.blurb: The Arevaci, Belli, Carpetani, Vettones, Vaccaei, Cantabri, Astures and Vascones.

realms.name: Carthage
realms.note: The Punic city-state with its African lands, western Sicily, Sardinia and the Phoenician towns of Spain.
realms.blurb: The dominant trading power of the western Mediterranean, backed by a navy few can match.

realms.name: Massylian Numidians
realms.note: The eastern Numidians; Zelalsan was the grandfather of Masinissa.
realms.blurb: The eastern Numidians; Zelalsan was the grandfather of Masinissa.

realms.name: Masaesylian Numidians
realms.note: The western Numidians, later Syphax's kingdom.
realms.blurb: The western Numidians, later Syphax's kingdom.

realms.name: Garamantes
realms.note: Desert farmers of the Fezzan, masters of the Saharan roads.
realms.blurb: Desert farmers of the Fezzan, masters of the Saharan roads.

realms.name: Ptolemaic Egypt
realms.note: Egypt with Cyrenaica, Coele-Syria (taken after Ipsus, 301 BC) and Lycian towns.
realms.blurb: Alexander's Macedonian generals still rule the Nile, richer than almost anyone.

realms.name: Kingdom of Kush
realms.note: The Kushite royal line passed through queens as well as kings.
realms.blurb: An African kingdom on the upper Nile, with its own pharaohs, iron industry, and pyramids.

realms.name: Kassander's Macedon
realms.note: Kassandros held Macedon, Thessaly and central Greece; his brother Pleistarchos was given Cilicia after Ipsus.
realms.blurb: Kassandros held Macedon, Thessaly and central Greece; his brother Pleistarchos was given Cilicia after Ipsus.

realms.name: Demetrios' Sea Kingdom
realms.note: Antigonos the One-Eyed fell at Ipsus (301 BC); his son Demetrios the Besieger kept the fleet, Cyprus, Tyre, Sidon, Corinth and the Peloponnese garrisons, and the islands.
realms.blurb: Antigonos the One-Eyed fell at Ipsus (301 BC); his son Demetrios the Besieger kept the fleet, Cyprus, Tyre, Sidon, Corinth and the Peloponnese garrisons, and the islands.

realms.name: Aetolian League
realms.note: A federal league with a yearly general (strategos).
realms.blurb: A federal league with a yearly general (strategos).

realms.name: Sparta
realms.note: King Areus I, of the Agiad house, reigned 309-265 BC.
realms.blurb: King Areus I, of the Agiad house, reigned 309-265 BC.

realms.name: Epirus
realms.note: In 300 BC Pyrrhos was a hostage at Alexandria, where he married Antigone, while Neoptolemos II held the throne; he was restored in 297 BC. The game starts him on it.
realms.blurb: In 300 BC Pyrrhos was a hostage at Alexandria, where he married Antigone, while Neoptolemos II held the throne; he was restored in 297 BC. The game starts him on it.

realms.name: Rhodes
realms.note: A free republic of merchants that had just withstood Demetrios' great siege (305-304 BC).
realms.blurb: A free republic of merchants that had just withstood Demetrios' great siege (305-304 BC).

realms.name: Cretan Cities
realms.note: Quarrelsome free cities, famous for their archers and mercenaries.
realms.blurb: Quarrelsome free cities, famous for their archers and mercenaries.

realms.name: Illyrian Kingdom
realms.note: Glaukias, king of the Taulantii, who had sheltered the boy Pyrrhos.
realms.blurb: Glaukias, king of the Taulantii, who had sheltered the boy Pyrrhos.

realms.name: Paeonia
realms.note: King Audoleon (c. 315-285 BC), whose daughter married Pyrrhos.
realms.blurb: King Audoleon (c. 315-285 BC), whose daughter married Pyrrhos.

realms.name: Odrysian Kingdom
realms.note: Seuthes III and his queen Berenike; their four sons are named in the Seuthopolis inscription.
realms.blurb: Seuthes III and his queen Berenike; their four sons are named in the Seuthopolis inscription.

realms.name: Getae
realms.note: Dromichaites, king of the Getae, captured Lysimachos in c. 292 BC and let him go.
realms.blurb: Dromichaites, king of the Getae, captured Lysimachos in c. 292 BC and let him go.

realms.name: Lysimachos' Kingdom
realms.note: After Ipsus (301 BC) Lysimachos added western and central Asia Minor to Thrace. In 302 BC he had married Amastris of Heraclea.
realms.blurb: After Ipsus (301 BC) Lysimachos added western and central Asia Minor to Thrace. In 302 BC he had married Amastris of Heraclea.

realms.name: Byzantium
realms.note: A free city holding the Bosporus and its grain ships.
realms.blurb: A free city holding the Bosporus and its grain ships.

realms.name: Bithynia
realms.note: Zipoites, who fought off Lysimachos' generals and took the title of king in 297 BC.
realms.blurb: Zipoites, who fought off Lysimachos' generals and took the title of king in 297 BC.

realms.name: Heraclea Pontica
realms.note: The tyrant house of Klearchos; Amastris, their mother, had married Lysimachos.
realms.blurb: The tyrant house of Klearchos; Amastris, their mother, had married Lysimachos.

realms.name: Pontus
realms.note: Mithridates the Founder fled Antigonos in 302 BC to Kimiata in Paphlagonia, the seed of the kingdom of Pontus.
realms.blurb: Mithridates the Founder fled Antigonos in 302 BC to Kimiata in Paphlagonia, the seed of the kingdom of Pontus.

realms.name: Cappadocia
realms.note: Ariarathes II won back his father's Cappadocia c. 301 BC with Armenian help.
realms.blurb: Ariarathes II won back his father's Cappadocia c. 301 BC with Armenian help.

realms.name: Armenia
realms.note: The Orontid kings of Armenia, Sophene and Commagene, nominally under the Seleucids.
realms.blurb: The Orontid kings of Armenia, Sophene and Commagene, nominally under the Seleucids.

realms.name: Atropatene
realms.note: Northern Media, which Atropates, satrap under Alexander, kept as a kingdom of its own.
realms.blurb: Northern Media, which Atropates, satrap under Alexander, kept as a kingdom of its own.

realms.name: Kartli (Caucasian Iberia)
realms.note: Parnavaz, remembered as the first king of Kartli (from c. 299 BC).
realms.blurb: Parnavaz, remembered as the first king of Kartli (from c. 299 BC).

realms.name: Colchis
realms.note: Kuji, eristavi of Colchis, Parnavaz's ally in the Georgian chronicles.
realms.blurb: Kuji, eristavi of Colchis, Parnavaz's ally in the Georgian chronicles.

realms.name: Bosporan Kingdom
realms.note: Spartokos III, of the house that ruled the Cimmerian Bosporus and fed Athens with grain.
realms.blurb: Spartokos III, of the house that ruled the Cimmerian Bosporus and fed Athens with grain.

realms.name: Scythians
realms.note: Agaros, a Scythian king named by Diodorus for 309 BC.
realms.blurb: Agaros, a Scythian king named by Diodorus for 309 BC.

realms.name: Sarmatians
realms.note: Iranian nomads east of the Don, with the Maeotian farmers of the Kuban.
realms.blurb: Iranian nomads east of the Don, with the Maeotian farmers of the Kuban.

realms.name: Seleucid Kingdom
realms.note: Seleukos Nikator, master of Babylon, Iran and (after Ipsus) northern Syria, where he founded Antioch in 300 BC.
realms.blurb: The largest of Alexander's successor kingdoms, stretching deep into the east.

realms.name: Nabataeans
realms.note: Nabataean queens ruled beside their husbands and appear on the coins.
realms.blurb: Desert traders controlling the incense routes, centred on their rock-cut capital.

realms.name: Lihyan
realms.note: The kingdom of Dedan on the Incense Road.
realms.blurb: The kingdom of Dedan on the Incense Road.

realms.name: Saba
realms.note: The oldest of the incense kingdoms, whose dam made Marib an oasis.
realms.blurb: The oldest of the incense kingdoms, whose dam made Marib an oasis.

realms.name: Ma'in
realms.note: The Minaeans, the great caravan traders of the incense.
realms.blurb: The Minaeans, the great caravan traders of the incense.

realms.note: The land of frankincense.
